## GoMeet PWA — System Design Summary

### Core Architecture Decision
This is a **web compilation layer**, not a new product. ~95% of the Flutter codebase is unchanged. All changes are confined to four areas: Firebase init fix, package stubs, PWA shell config, and responsive layout additions.

### Key Technical Decisions (incorporating your choices)

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| **Web Renderer** | Auto (HTML mobile / CanvasKit desktop) | Optimises bundle size per device without manual override |
| **App Check** | reCAPTCHA v3 — included in v1 | Monitoring mode during QA → enforced before public launch |
| **CI/CD** | Manual deploy | `flutter build web --release` + `firebase deploy` |
| **Backend** | Firebase only — no new API server | Existing Firestore + Auth + Storage; unchanged Security Rules |
| **Offline** | App shell cached; live data requires network | Service worker via `offline-first` Flutter build strategy |

### 5-Phase Implementation Sequence
1. **Build unblocked** — Fix Firebase init, add package stubs, zero build errors
2. **Core flows** — Auth, profile creation, swipe/match, chat all working in Chrome
3. **PWA shell** — manifest.json, icons, service worker, Lighthouse PWA ≥ 90
4. **Responsive layouts** — Tablet breakpoints for Discover (600px) and Chat (768px)
5. **Polish & deploy** — App Check enforced, install CTA, cache headers, final Lighthouse run

### 7 Open Questions to Resolve Before Implementation
The most critical blockers are: Firebase web config values (#1), reCAPTCHA v3 site key (#2), and Firestore Security Rules platform audit (#3).
